sections.html:
Waterloo serves as the Black Hawk County seat, in northeast Iowa, with the Cedar River running between its east and west sides. Cedar Falls, home of the University of Northern Iowa, is its twin city next door. The 2020 census counted 67,314 people, making Waterloo the eighth-largest city in Iowa, and the metro area has about 170,000 residents.

Buyers often compare Waterloo with Cedar Falls, Evansdale, Hudson, Raymond, Elk Run Heights, Gilbertville and Washburn, so price and condition get measured against those places.

sections.h2: The Factory City and its older houses
sections.html:
Factory work built this city. The settlement began as Prairie Rapids Crossing in 1845 and became Waterloo when Charles Mullan petitioned for a post office. The city incorporated in 1868, and population jumped from 8,490 in 1895 to 33,097 in 1915. The Waterloo Gasoline Engine Company began making Waterloo Boy tractors in 1893, and Rath Packing arrived in the same period. Much of the older housing traces to those decades.

The boom did not hold evenly. John Deere cut about 10,000 jobs in the 1980s farm recession and now employs roughly a third of its peak workforce, with more layoffs in 2024 and 2025. The Rath plant closed in the 1980s, taking about 2,500 jobs, and the city lost an estimated 14 percent of its population that decade. Owners who held houses through all of that often face a mix of older homes and slower appreciation.

One manufacturer accounts for 4,300 of those jobs, so news from John Deere can ripple through the local housing market.

Across 2020 to 2024, 62.1 percent of homes were owner-occupied and the median home value was $152,600. Median gross rent is $923, median household income is $57,480, and households average 2.25 people.

About 38 percent of occupied homes are not owner-occupied, so a fair share of the houses on any block may belong to landlords. That shapes who your neighbors are and who might buy your house.

The June 2008 flood is the benchmark. It was the largest on record for the Waterloo and Cedar Falls area, with a peak discharge of 112,000 cubic feet per second at the Waterloo gage on June 11. The Great Flood of 1993 was another major event.

The city has put money into its levees. After the Army Corps identified deficiencies in 2016, Waterloo spent just over $8 million on two phases of upgrades, finished in 2022 and 2024, and the system is again eligible for federal flood protection programs. An October 2025 report put the East and Northwest segments at full compliance, with the Southwest segment due to finish by the end of 2025.

Find out from your insurance agent if your address sits in a mapped floodplain, because a financed buyer must then carry coverage. A cash buyer can skip that lender requirement.

sections.h2: Winter wear on roofs and furnaces
sections.html:
Monthly mean temperatures run from 18.5 degrees F in January to 73.6 degrees F in July, and the record low is minus 34 degrees F, reached in 1962 and again in 2009. Winter snowfall averages 35.3 inches, with heavier rain in spring and summer.

Spring melt and heavy rain are the seasons to watch for basement moisture. With winters that cold, buyers look closely at furnace age and attic insulation.

Waterloo requires registration of every rental unit, even a vacant one. The program applies to dwellings that are not eligible for the Iowa homestead credit and are not the owner's home, and landlords must name a responsible local agent.

The registration fee is $25 per unit, the late fee rises to $50 per unit on January 1, and the annual deadline is November 1 for a permit running January 1 to December 31. A newly purchased rental must be registered within 30 days, so a buyer will need to register right away. Ask the City Clerk at 319-291-4323 how your registration is handled at a sale before you close.

sections.h2: City repair programs versus an as-is sale
sections.html:
Waterloo Community Development runs owner-occupied rehabilitation, emergency repair, Healthy Homes and lead hazard programs, plus rental rehabilitation loans and down payment help for qualifying buyers. The office is at 620 Mulberry Street, Suite 202, and its number is 319-291-4429.

Those programs are worth a call if you plan to stay. If you plan to leave, the question is whether repair funding and contractor time fit your timeline. Call the office for eligibility rules and award amounts. Ask whether a repair loan would have to be paid off at closing, and whether work in progress affects the sale date.

The Waterloo Community School District covers nearly the entire city. Its public high schools are Waterloo West, Waterloo East and Expo High School, and private options include Waterloo Christian School and Columbus Catholic High School.

Hawkeye Community College is in Waterloo, and MercyOne Waterloo Medical Center and UnityPoint Allen Memorial Hospital anchor health care. Interstate 380 ends at Waterloo, U.S. 20, 63 and 218 and Iowa 21 serve the area, and the Metropolitan Transit Authority of Black Hawk County runs local buses Monday through Saturday.

Black Hawk County sends two bills a year. The September 1 payment is late after September 30, and the March 1 payment is late after March 31. Late balances grow by 1.5 percent monthly, and the county holds its tax sale on the third Monday of June.

Iowa's transfer tax works out to 80 cents for every $500 above the first $500, and a partial $500 counts as a full one. The recorder gets a declaration of value along with the deed. If taxes are owed, the closing pays them out of your proceeds.

sections.h2: Selling a house that needs work
sections.html:
Deferred repairs leave three paths: list for a buyer who will renovate, tap a city repair program if you qualify and mean to stay, or take a cash offer as-is. In the cash route you describe the house, get an offer, and the title company takes care of the deed, payoffs and recording on the day you pick.

Round up the deed, a tax statement, mortgage payoff figures and, for a rental, the registration papers. Floodplain houses should come with whatever insurance or levee information you hold.

Sellers in Waterloo include heirs with an older house from the factory decades, landlords ready to leave the rental business, and owners who would rather not invest in a new roof or furnace before moving. Each of them benefits from a clear closing date and a payoff figure in writing.

faqs.q: Do Waterloo landlords have to register a rental before selling it?
faqs.a: Yes, for as long as you own it. The $25 per-unit fee is due November 1 and covers empty units too. A buyer registers within 30 days after buying.

faqs.q: When are Black Hawk County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payments fall on September 1 and March 1. Anything unpaid is delinquent after September 30 or March 31.

faqs.q: Is Waterloo still at risk of Cedar River flooding?
faqs.a: Some risk remains. The city finished about $8 million in levee upgrades in 2022 and 2024, but your address may still sit in a mapped floodplain, so ask your insurance agent.

faqs.q: What is a typical home value in Waterloo?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes had a median value of $152,600 across 2020 to 2024. Condition and location can put yours well off that figure.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Waterloo house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Options include selling as-is, listing to a renovator, or using a city repair program if you qualify and plan to stay.
